import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Group by the year of the data snapshot and the dog's gender,
# then count the number of dogs for each group.
# Each row represents a unique dog-year observation, so .size() gives the count.
dog_counts_by_year_gender = df.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'SexHundLang']).size().reset_index(name='Anzahl Hunde')

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a line plot to visualize the trend of dog registrations over years,
# broken down by dog gender.
sns.lineplot(
    data=dog_counts_by_year_gender,
    x='StichtagDatJahr',
    y='Anzahl Hunde',
    hue='SexHundLang',
    marker='o', # Add circles at each data point for clarity
    palette={'männlich': '#4CAF50', 'weiblich': '#FF6F61'} # Custom color palette
)

# Add a descriptive title to the plot
plt.title('Number of Registered Dogs in Zurich by Year and Gender', fontsize=16, weight='bold')

# Label the x-axis
plt.xlabel('Year of Data Snapshot', fontsize=12)

# Label the y-axis
plt.ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)

# Ensure all unique years are shown on the x-axis and format them as integers
plt.xticks(dog_counts_by_year_gender['StichtagDatJahr'].unique().astype(int))

# Add a legend to distinguish between genders, with a clear title
plt.legend(title='Dog Gender', loc='upper left', frameon=True, borderpad=1)

# Add a grid for better readability of the trends
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Improve layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
